summary: Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist who studied at Berlin, Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, and others. He worked at the India Office Library and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau (1833–1872).

Adolf Holtzmann the Elder was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. From 1852 to 1870, he served as professor of German literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University.

Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Zurich, Leipzig, and Tübingen, learning under Rudolf von Roth and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He spent his career at the University of Zurich, eventually serving as Ordinarius from 1893 to 1914.

Adolf Kirchhoff was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Böckh. He taught at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium before serving as ordinary professor at the University of Berlin from 1865 until around 1908.
Adolf Noreen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University and under August Leskien in 1879. He subsequently held an academic post at Uppsala University from around 1887 to 1919.

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology and linguistics and studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Collège de France (1838), the École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), and served as librarian at the Palace of Fontainebleau from 1873.

Adriaan Scharpé was an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Jan Gonda at Utrecht University. He later held posts as assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978) and professor at Ghent University (~1958–1983).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology, having studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He lectured at the European School of Culture and Theology and became a Senior Fellow at the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation in 2019.
Adrienne Wallman works in religious and Buddhist studies. As attested in 2026, she is a PhD student at Lancaster University studying under Mark Hurst.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies who conducted research at the Universities of Oslo (1993) and Bonn (1995). She has held academic posts at the University of Warsaw, attested in 2008 and 2026.

Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He served as a gymnasium teacher at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and became a Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1839.

Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Vienna. He taught at Delhi, Banaras Hindu University, Tokyo, and Kyoto, and served as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny is a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology who studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University. She held affiliations with Cornell University (~2008–2010) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery, earning the Geshe Lharampa degree. He founded the Atsagat and Gunzechoyney datsans and taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Ahmad Hasan Dani was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at the University of London. He held posts at Dhaka, Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam University, where he became Dean in 1971.

Aiko Okoshi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1970–1975). She was appointed full-time lecturer at Kindai University in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho after graduating from Bedford College. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010) before becoming abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery around 2010.
Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist studies practitioner educated at the University of Cambridge who studied under Nai Boonman and Ajahn Chah. He became abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery around 1995.
Ajahn Khemadhammo is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended the Drama Centre London and studied under Ajahn Chah from around 1972 to 1977.
Ajahn Pasanno is a Buddhist studies teacher who studied under Ajahn Chah from around 1975 to 1992. He served as founding co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery from around 1996 to 2018.
